_comment: Built-in MCP hands, seeded into the registry at startup. Edit + restart to change.
_why_no_stdio_hands: Mark 3 shipped two stdio hands — a filesystem server rooted at C:\Users\user
and C:\Code, and Playwright driving msedge. Both spawned a subprocess on the
machine running the backend. On a single-user desktop that machine was the
user's own, so 'the filesystem hand can read your files' was the feature.
Hosted, that same code reads OUR container's filesystem, shared by every
tenant, and hands a model process execution on the server. The paths were
Windows-only and msedge does not exist on Linux, so they would fail — but
failing is not the same as being safe, and they must not come back by
accident. Remote HTTP MCP servers are the supported path: they run on
someone else's machine, under the same consent gate.
mcp_stdio.py is kept and unmounted. DIRECTION names it the template for the
LSP bridge — the same async JSON-RPC shape with Content-Length framing.
